note: Saturday 31 Oct 2026 07:02 SGT weekend refresh. Markets closed since Friday 2026-10-30's sharp risk-off US close (S&P -1.82%, VIX +12.9% to 19.42); Fear & Greed, breadth and fund-flow data below reflect that Friday close and the latest published weekly flow cut (week ended 2026-10-28), which itself predates the full Friday reaction.

fearGreed.note: Headline value (26, up from 16 a week ago) is corroborated across three independent citations of CNN's own index (CNN.com 10/30 article, TokenPost, a weekly-recap substack) plus feargreedtracker.com's CNN-methodology mirror. CNN's own site still returns 403/451 to automated fetch, so the 7 sub-component readings are estimated: a third-party mirror (aiStockSelection) published a full 7-component table on 10/30 that was still showing ~35 (essentially unchanged from Thursday's 36 close), i.e. not yet refreshed for Friday's selloff; the components above take that table's relative shape/signals and scale them down to be consistent with the press-corroborated 26 headline. Treat individual component values as directionally right but approximate.

metrics.value: 6 of 11 sectors majority-above: Health Care 81.7%, Energy 66.7%, Info Tech 64.9%, Financials 63.2%, Materials 61.5%, Consumer Staples 60.6%; weakest are Real Estate 23.3% and Utilities 16.1%; S&P-wide average ~53.3% (October 2026 composite reading, not Oct-30-specific)

breadth.note: Breadth cracked hard into Friday's close: the short-term 50-DMA participation measure collapsed from roughly two-thirds of the index to about a third in two sessions, while the slower 200-DMA measure held up much better (~59%) -- a classic 'fast air pocket, slower trend damage' pattern. Nasdaq internals were far worse than NYSE's (3-to-1 decliners vs 1.8-to-1), reflecting how concentrated the selloff was in mega-cap AI/semiconductor names (Intel, Amazon, Alphabet), while some defensive sectors (Health Care, Real Estate) reportedly outperformed on the day itself even though their longer-term 200-DMA readings diverge sharply (Health Care strong, Real Estate weak). The McClellan Oscillator and advance-decline-line figures above are the most recent published and predate Friday's drop, so they likely overstate current breadth health.

flows.period: week ending 2026-10-28 (Wednesday EPFR/Lipper cut -- newly published since the week-ending-Oct-21 'Enter the Dragon' report used in the prior update. This cut predates Thursday 10/29's Alphabet-driven drop and Friday 10/30's much sharper AI-led selloff, which will first show up in the week-ending-Nov-4 release)
flows.narrative: Global equity funds booked a sixth straight week of inflows but at a much slower pace (+$10.2B vs +$25.1B the week before) as US funds flipped to their first outflow in three weeks (-$6.65B) ahead of hyperscaler earnings, while Asia (Japan's record Topix rebalance, Korea's chip rally) and Europe absorbed most of the money. Cash funds swung hard into outflows, bond inflows cooled to a six-week low, and gold ETFs booked a second outflow week in the last seven as bullion wobbled -- all before Thursday/Friday's sharper risk-off break that this cut does not yet capture.

regions.note: First weekly outflow in three weeks (EPFR/Reuters), ahead of Amazon/Intel/Alphabet earnings; Lipper's cap breakdown: large-cap -$3.8B, mid-cap -$2.11B, small-cap -$832M, multi-cap -$303M.
